hypothesis: Every MDBX operation calls txn_execute, which takes the transaction mutex and reads the SeqCst timed_out latch; together ~8% of heavy-phase server CPU (>::lock 7.4% + atomic_load 1.1% in champ-symbols). Both latches are one-way, so Acquire/Release is sufficient and replaces full barriers (dmb ish on aarch64) with ldar/stlr. Expect a few % on heavy, most on m9g/Graviton5.
llm_commentary: Relaxing the MDBX one-way latches from SeqCst to Acquire/Release (commit abb594c223) is neutral: m9g 4.72→4.70s, m8azn-3xl 4.51→4.54s, both inside run spread, including on Graviton5 where SeqCst lowers to a dmb ish barrier. That localises the ~8% the champion profile attributed to this area: 7.4% of it sat in TransactionPtr::lock's try_lock (an uncontended mutex CAS per database operation) and only ~1% in the timed_out load, so changing the load's ordering could not move the total. Removing the mutex itself is not available: TransactionPtr and Cursor are both Sync, so it is what serialises concurrent MDBX calls on one transaction, and dropping it would break the library's contract rather than just risk it. The commit is still correct and slightly cheaper, but it is not a measurable win on this workload; keeping the champion unchanged.
